Put it in a new migration file, `migrations/0008_add_customer_phone.sql`. Don't edit `migrations/0007_add_customers.sql`.

The project's memory store says files in `migrations/` have already been applied in production, so you never edit one. Each change gets a new file with the next 4-digit number. Changing 0007 wouldn't touch databases that have already run it, so production and new environments would end up with different schemas.

Following the style of `0003_add_ledger_ref.sql`:

```sql
ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN phone TEXT;
```

Leave the column nullable. A `NOT NULL` column with no default will fail on a table that already has rows. If you need it to be required, add it as nullable, backfill the existing rows, then add the constraint.

I noticed something else while looking: 0007 creates the email column with a typo, as `emial`. If you want to fix that, do it in a migration too (e.g. `ALTER TABLE customers RENAME COLUMN emial TO email;`), either in 0008 or in its own file. Nothing in `src/` references `customers` yet, so no app code would break. Tell me if you want me to create the file.
